title: Splitting orthogonals: extensions, retracts and diagonal fillers
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Write $U\perp_1 V$ if every short exact sequence $0\to V\to E\to U\to0$ splits, meaning that its epimorphism admits a section. For any class $\mathcal S$ of objects put ${}^{\perp_1}\mathcal S=\{U:U\perp_1 V\text{ for every }V\in\mathcal S\}$ and $\mathcal S^{\perp_1}=\{V:U\perp_1 V\text{ for every }U\in\mathcal S\}$. Both these classes contain zero and are closed under retracts and extensions: if $X$ is a retract of $Y$ in the class then $X$ belongs to it, and if $0\to X\to Y\to Z\to0$ is short exact with $X,Z$ in the class then $Y$ belongs to it. Moreover, if $i:A\to B$ is monic and $p:X\to Y$ is epic with $(\operatorname{Coker}i)\perp_1(\operatorname{Ker}p)$, every pair $a:A\to X$, $b:B\to Y$ satisfying $pa=bi$ has a morphism $d:B\to X$ with $di=a$ and $pd=b$.

proof.text: Fix the abelian category and use functional composition throughout. Short exact means monic first arrow, epic second arrow, and equality of image and kernel, as in [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. In a short exact sequence $0\to V\xrightarrow{k}E\xrightarrow{q}U\to0$, $q$ is a cokernel of $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel](a), and $k$ is a kernel of $q$: its identification with the image follows from monicity and exactness. Splitting can be tested by a retraction of $k$. Indeed, if $qs=1$, factor $1-sq$ through the kernel as $kr=1-sq$; cancellation of $k$ gives $rk=1$. Conversely, if $rk=1$, factor $1-kr$ through the cokernel as $sq=1-kr$; cancellation of $q$ gives $qs=1$. These formulas use only the displayed kernel and cokernel universal properties.

source.place: Tag 010E (definition-exact); abelian-category kernel/cokernel conventions; elementary splitting calculation using the extension of Tag 010J (definition-extension).

proof.text: Here is the pullback construction used below, with its short exactness verified rather than assumed. For the sequence of step 1 and any $h:W\to U$, let $F=E\times_UW$, $u:F\to E$, $v:F\to W$. It exists as the kernel of $(q,-h):E\oplus W\to U$, by the biproduct and kernel universal properties [def-sp-abelian]. The map $\ell:V\to F$ is specified by $u\ell=k$, $v\ell=0$. Any map killed by $v$ factors uniquely through $\ell$, since its $E$ component is killed by $q$; thus $\ell$ is the kernel of $v$. For $w:T\to W$, the epimorphism criterion [lem-sp-abelian-refinements](a) lifts $hw$ through $q$ after an epimorphism $\rho:T'\to T$; the resulting pair of maps to $E,W$ gives a lift of $w\rho$ to $F$. The same criterion makes $v$ epic. Thus $0\to V\to F\to W\to0$ is short exact. This is a three-line universal-property/refinement argument, not a new lemma node.

source.place: Tag 010I (section-extensions), pullback construction after Tag 010K (definition-ext-group); the epimorphic-refinement criterion is Tag 08N5 (lemma-check-exactness-fibre-product).

proof.text: We will also use the following quotient construction, proved here from the cited snake lemma. Suppose $0\to K\xrightarrow{k}T\xrightarrow{q}B\to0$ is short exact and $j:A\to T$ has monic composite $i=qj:A\to B$; then $j$ is monic because $j a=0$ implies $i a=qj a=0$, and monicity of $i$ gives $a=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-snake-lemma-abelian] to the exact top row $0\to A\xrightarrow{1}A\to0$ (the three objects are $0,A,A$), bottom row $0\to K\xrightarrow{k}T\xrightarrow{q}B\to0$, and vertical maps $0:0\to K$, $j:A\to T$, $i:A\to B$. Their kernels are all zero. Their cokernels are $K,Q=\operatorname{Coker}j,C=\operatorname{Coker}i$. The snake sequence therefore gives $0\to K\xrightarrow{\bar k}Q\xrightarrow{\bar q}C\to0$, with $\bar k=\pi k$ for $\pi:T\to Q$ and $\bar q\pi=cq$ for $c:B\to C$. Exactness at $K$ makes $\bar k$ monic; the snake lemma gives $\bar q$ epic since the bottom right arrow $q$ is epic. This proves all the asserted short exactness, without any splitting assumption.

source.place: Tag 010H (lemma-snake), exact six-term kernel/cokernel sequence and the right endpoint assertion; applied to the explicitly specified two rows.

proof.text: Zero is orthogonal in both variables. In an extension $0\to V\xrightarrow{k}E\to0\to0$, exactness says that the monomorphism $k$ has image all of $E$, hence is also epic; in an abelian category a morphism that is both monic and epic is an isomorphism, so the sequence splits. In an extension $0\to0\to E\xrightarrow{q}U\to0$, the map $q$ is the cokernel of the zero map $0\to E$ by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel](a), and therefore is an isomorphism (the identity of $E$ has the same cokernel universal property). Thus both sequences split. This works for every object tested against the class, including an empty class.

source.place: Tag 010J (definition-extension); elementary zero-object and cokernel-universal-property calculation.

proof.text: For left retract closure, let $s:X\to Y$, $r:Y\to X$ satisfy $rs=1_X$, and suppose $Y\perp_1 V$. Given an extension $0\to V\to E\xrightarrow{q}X\to0$, pull it back along $r$ using step 2. Its quotient is $Y$, so choose a section $t:Y\to E\times_XY$ by the assumed orthogonality. If $u:E\times_XY\to E$ is the other projection, then $quts=rs=1_X$. Hence the original extension splits, proving $X\perp_1V$. Quantify this argument over all $V\in\mathcal S$.

source.place: Tag 010I (section-extensions), pullback operation; elementary section composition after step 2.

proof.text: For right retract closure with the same $s,r$, suppose $U\perp_1Y$. Push any extension $0\to X\xrightarrow{k}E\to U\to0$ out along $s:X\to Y$. The cited [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-short-exact-sequence] gives $0\to Y\xrightarrow{k'}E'\to U\to0$ and a map $v:E\to E'$ with $vk=k's$. Orthogonality and step 1 give a retraction $t:E'\to Y$ of $k'$. Then $rtv:E\to X$ retracts $k$, since $rtvk=rs=1_X$, so step 1 splits the original sequence. Quantify over all $U\in\mathcal S$.

source.place: Tag 010I (section-extensions), pushout operation; elementary retraction composition after the cited pushed-out short exact sequence.

proof.text: For left extension closure, fix $V\in\mathcal S$ and $0\to X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z\to0$ with $X\perp_1V$ and $Z\perp_1V$. Given $0\to V\xrightarrow{k}E\xrightarrow{q}Y\to0$, step 2 pulls it back along $f$, and $X\perp_1V$ supplies a section. Its $E$ component is $t:X\to E$ with $qt=f$. Step 3 applied to $j=t$, $i=f$ gives $0\to V\xrightarrow{\pi k}E/tX\to Z\to0$. Here $\operatorname{Coker}f$ is identified with $Z$ by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel](a). This sequence splits by $Z\perp_1V$, so step 1 supplies $R:E/tX\to V$ with $R\pi k=1_V$. The composite $R\pi$ retracts $k$, and step 1 splits the original extension. All quotient exactness is the snake calculation in step 3, not a new orthogonality node.

source.place: Tag 010I (section-extensions), pullback operation; agent closure argument using the explicit snake-lemma consequence established in step 3 (Tag 010H).

proof.text: For right extension closure, fix $U\in\mathcal S$ and $0\to X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z\to0$ with $U\perp_1X$ and $U\perp_1Z$. Push $0\to Y\xrightarrow{k}E\xrightarrow{q}U\to0$ out along $g:Y\to Z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-short-exact-sequence] this gives $0\to Z\xrightarrow{k'}E'\xrightarrow{q'}U\to0$, with $v:E\to E'$, $vk=k'g$, $q'v=q$. The map $v$ is epic: if two maps out of $E'$ agree after $v$, their composites with $k'$ agree after the epic $g$, hence agree; the pushout uniqueness then makes the two maps equal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-kernel-iso] to the square with top $g$, left $k$, right $k'$, bottom $v$. Its left side $k$ is monic, so $\ker g\simeq\ker v$; since $f$ identifies $X$ with $\ker g$, this identifies $kf:X\to E$ with $\ker v$. Consequently $0\to X\xrightarrow{kf}E\xrightarrow{v}E'\to0$ is short exact. Choose a section $s:U\to E'$ of $q'$ by $U\perp_1Z$, and pull this last sequence back along $s$ by step 2. It is an extension of $U$ by $X$, so $U\perp_1X$ gives a section and hence a map $t:U\to E$ with $vt=s$. Now $qt=q'vt=q's=1_U$. This splits the original extension and proves right extension closure.

source.place: Tag 010I (section-extensions), pushout and pullback operations; Tags 08N4 (lemma-cartesian-cocartesian) and 08N3 (lemma-cartesian-kernel) as combined in the cited pushout-kernel isomorphism; agent closure argument.

proof.text: For the diagonal-filler assertion, put $K=\operatorname{Ker}p$, $C=\operatorname{Coker}i$ and form $T=X\times_YB$ with projections $u:T\to X$, $q:T\to B$. Since $p$ is epic and $K\to X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ is exact at $X$, [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel](a) makes $p$ a cokernel of the kernel inclusion, so $0\to K\to X\xrightarrow{p}Y\to0$ is short exact. Step 2 therefore gives $0\to K\xrightarrow{k}T\xrightarrow{q}B\to0$. Commutativity $pa=bi$ gives $j:A\to T$ with $uj=a$, $qj=i$. Since $i$ is monic, step 3 gives $0\to K\xrightarrow{\pi k}Q\xrightarrow{\bar q}C\to0$, where $Q=\operatorname{Coker}j$ and $\pi:T\to Q$. The assumption $C\perp_1K$ splits this specific extension. By step 1 choose $R:Q\to K$ with $R\pi k=1_K$. Set $r=R\pi:T\to K$; then $rk=1_K$ and $rj=0$ because $\pi j=0$.

source.place: Tag 010J (definition-extension) and Tag 010I (section-extensions), pullback; agent construction of the obstruction extension using step 3 (Tag 010H).

proof.text: Finish the lift using only cokernel factorization. The morphism $1_T-kr$ kills $k$, since $rk=1_K$. Because $q$ is a cokernel of $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel](a), there is a unique $w:B\to T$ with $wq=1_T-kr$. Now $qwq=q$, so epic cancellation of $q$ yields $qw=1_B$. Also $wi=wqj=(1_T-kr)j=j$, using $rj=0$. Define $d=uw:B\to X$. Then $di=uj=a$ and $pd=puw=bqw=b$, by the pullback relation $pu=bq$. This is the required filler, and steps 4--8 have already established both closure assertions.
